Numbers randomized and per-arm analyzed counts are not printed. Survey enrollment and overall completion are not randomization counts. Full three-arm model sizes are retained in study records and model notes, not substituted for unknown two-arm contrast counts.
S2 recommendation-quality models use 372 participant observations, while the experiment and correctness models have 373; no reason for the discrepancy is reported.
Participant-level outcome SDs, treatment-arm means, and standardized effects are absent from the tabulated quality models. No SDs or means were derived from coefficients, SEs, or figures.

The between-person similarity analyses print neither numerical arm levels nor uncertainty nor their participant/idea counts. The shared-reference construction also creates dependence between participant similarity values.
Appendix D does not identify the idea-list creativity evaluator or provide the cited results table. The corresponding estimate uses measure null; the fixed measure vocabulary has no unknown category.
The available source states preregistration and names paper-primary outcomes, but the embargoed registration is not on file. Preregistered primary status remains not_stated.
The individual question-level effects in the quality figures cannot be mapped to named questions or transcribed numerically; only their text-reported average effects are retained.
AI-configuration comparisons print F-test p-values but not F statistics, degrees of freedom, effect differences, or their SEs.

The screening form excludes brand-choice correctness as an analytic outcome. It is retained here as convergent under the extraction instruction to extract tests with right answers; it must remain outside pooled creativity estimates.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-09. Read the complete markdown conversion and the PDF tables, figures, and Appendices A-E. All numeric sources were checked with pymupdf text extraction; table finding and in-memory page rendering were also used. Only the named extraction file was written. The studies use disjoint participants, as Section 2, PDF p. 10 (printed p. 6), states; the screening form identifies no overlap with other papers. Assignment was individual, stratified by gender, location, tenure, openness to innovation, and native English status. All participants completed a no-AI assessment before random assignment, so these are between-person experiments, not randomized-order crossover designs. The source reports 852 survey respondents and 758 completers (PDF p. 9, footnote 3), without an explicit randomized denominator. Each full-sample specification is retained separately for auditability; specifications and outcomes within a study reuse participants. The paper calls human-graded quality primary in S1 (PDF p. 13) and correctness primary in S2 (PDF p. 18); those statements do not establish preregistered primacy. S2 recommendation quality is included as usefulness of innovative business actions, supported by the task in Appendix A and the rubric in Appendix B. No raw-data calculations, standardized effects, converted units, inferred arm counts, figure digitization, or reconstructed means were used. Source quotes preserve printed decimal precision, including trailing zeros; numeric JSON fields are numbers. Missing statistics are null. The positive text magnitude for the pooled correctness decrease explicitly uses Control minus AI in difference_is.
